title: Microsoft 365 Apps admin center: Update Repair in Inventory
summary: Hold: the remote Repair path starts at a banner button without telling administrators which page to open first. Microsoft documents that button on Home and Inventory. The behaviour, rollout dates and manual repair command are supported; the licensing model also understates the published Inventory entitlement.

claims.fix: The path stops on the right page before the setup control. Set controls[0].ui.path and its rendered counterpart to 'Inventory > Get started', and cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365-apps/best-practices/roadmap-to-modern-management, which says 'Navigate to Inventory and choose Get started to enable the feature.'

claims.claim: A tenant new to Inventory completes a one-step setup.

The existing path starts inside a page at its banner rather than identifying the navigation page containing it. The cited Update Repair page documents the banner on Inventory.

claims.quote: Your user must be assigned to one of the following subscription plans: ... Microsoft 365 Business Standard ... Microsoft 365 Business Premium ... Office 365 E3 ... Office 365 E5 ... Microsoft 365 E3 ... Microsoft 365 E5
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to 'included'. Replace licensing.notes with 'Update Repair uses Inventory, whose licensing requirements say the signed-in user must have a listed plan, such as Microsoft 365 E3 or E5. Microsoft Learn publishes no licence or meter specific to Update Repair as of November 2026.' Remove the final Open questions bullet questioning the applicability of the product-level requirement. Keep the existing Inventory citation.
